input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get the best speed possible?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I’ll do my best, but I get a bit flustered with step-by-step instructions, especially if they’re technical. Could you please keep things as simple as possible and let me know if I’m doing things right along the way? I really want to make sure I get excellent internet speed. What should I do first?

At the top of my screen, I see just one bar for signal, it says 2G, and there’s a little icon that looks like a lock with “VPN” next to it. My battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon. Is that okay, or is something wrong?

Okay, I’ve changed the setting so my phone now prefers 4G and 5G. At the top, it now shows four bars for signal and says 5G. The VPN icon is still there, though. What should I do next? Will this make my internet excellent now?

Alright, I’ve turned off the VPN. Now at the top, it still shows four bars and 5G, but the VPN icon is gone. Is there anything else I should do, or should I check my internet speed now? I really want to make sure it’s excellent.
Oh dear, I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I thought everything was set up right since it shows 5G and four bars. What should I do now?
It looks like my mobile data is turned on—I see the little data icon at the top of my screen. I’m not sure why it still says there’s no connection when I try the speed test. What should I do next?

I restarted my phone like you said, and I waited until I saw the 5G and four bars again. But when I tried the speed test, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? What else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.

I checked, and my APN name is set to “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I don’t really understand what any of that means. Should I still reset it, or is it already correct? I just want to make sure I do the right thing to get excellent internet speed.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t anything working? I just want excellent internet speed. What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get the best speed possible?

I can help you troubleshoot and improve your mobile data speed. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and guide you through the steps to improve your mobile data speed.
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you, John. I’ve found your account and confirmed your line is active with the Premium Plan, which includes 15GB of data per month. You’ve used about 8.7GB so far, so you still have data available.

To help improve your mobile data speed, I’ll need to guide you through a few checks and adjustments on your phone. Are you able to follow step-by-step instructions on your device? If so, please let me know, and I’ll start with the first step.

I’ll do my best, but I get a bit flustered with step-by-step instructions, especially if they’re technical. Could you please keep things as simple as possible and let me know if I’m doing things right along the way? I really want to make sure I get excellent internet speed. What should I do first?

Absolutely, John! I’ll keep each step simple and clear, and I’ll check in with you after each one to make sure you’re comfortable before moving on.

Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar to see if there are any obvious issues (like Airplane Mode being on or a weak signal). 

On your phone, can you look at the very top of your screen and tell me what icons you see? For example, do you see an airplane, how many bars of signal, and does it say 4G, 5G, or something else? If you’re not sure, just describe what you see, and I’ll help you figure it out!
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

At the top of my screen, I see just one bar for signal, it says 2G, and there’s a little icon that looks like a lock with “VPN” next to it. My battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon. Is that okay, or is something wrong?

Thank you for describing what you see, John. Here’s what this means:
- One bar for signal means your connection is weak.
- “2G” is an older, much slower network—this is likely why your internet is slow.
- The “VPN” icon means your phone is using a Virtual Private Network, which can sometimes slow things down even more.

Let’s fix these one at a time. First, we’ll try to get you on a faster network (like 4G or 5G). 

Would you like me to guide you through changing your network setting to prefer 4G/5G? This should help improve your speed right away.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Okay, I’ve changed the setting so my phone now prefers 4G and 5G. At the top, it now shows four bars for signal and says 5G. The VPN icon is still there, though. What should I do next? Will this make my internet excellent now?

Great job, John! Switching to 5G with four bars is excellent and should give you much faster internet. The VPN icon means your phone is still using a Virtual Private Network, which can sometimes slow down your connection even if you have a strong signal.

To get the best possible speed, I recommend disconnecting the VPN. Would you like simple instructions on how to turn off the VPN on your phone? If you turn it off, your internet should be as fast as possible with your current plan and signal.

VPN disconnected successfully.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve turned off the VPN. Now at the top, it still shows four bars and 5G, but the VPN icon is gone. Is there anything else I should do, or should I check my internet speed now? I really want to make sure it’s excellent.

That’s perfect, John! With four bars of signal, 5G, and no VPN, your phone is set up for the best possible speed on your plan.

The next step is to check your internet speed to make sure everything is working as it should. Would you like instructions on how to run a speed test on your phone, or do you already have a speed test app you like to use? Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and I’ll guide you through it!
Speed test failed: No Connection.
Oh dear, I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. I thought everything was set up right since it shows 5G and four bars. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know, John. Sometimes, even if your phone shows 5G and full signal, there can be a small issue with your mobile data connection that needs a quick fix.

Let’s try a simple step: please check if your mobile data is turned ON in your phone’s settings. Sometimes it can be switched off by accident. 

Can you look in your phone’s settings and confirm if “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data” is turned ON? If you’re not sure how to check, let me know what type of phone you have (Android or iPhone), and I’ll give you easy instructions.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
It looks like my mobile data is turned on—I see the little data icon at the top of my screen. I’m not sure why it still says there’s no connection when I try the speed test. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking, John. Since your mobile data is ON and you have a strong 5G signal, but still can’t connect, the issue might be with your phone’s network settings or a temporary glitch.

Let’s try a simple fix: restarting your phone. This refreshes all connections and often solves these kinds of problems.

Please restart your phone now. After it turns back on, wait a moment for it to reconnect to the network (you should see the 5G and signal bars again), then try the speed test once more.

Let me know what happens after you restart and test your internet. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll try the next step together.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, and I waited until I saw the 5G and four bars again. But when I tried the speed test, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? What else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.

Thank you for your patience, John. I understand how frustrating this can be, and I’m here to help you step by step.

Since restarting didn’t fix the issue, the next thing we should check is your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. If these settings are incorrect, your phone can’t connect to the internet even if everything else looks right.

Would you like simple instructions on how to check or reset your APN settings? Resetting them to default is safe and often solves this problem. Let me know if you’d like to proceed, and I’ll guide you through it.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked, and my APN name is set to “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I don’t really understand what any of that means. Should I still reset it, or is it already correct? I just want to make sure I do the right thing to get excellent internet speed.

Thank you for checking, John. Sometimes, even if the APN name looks correct, there can be small errors that prevent your internet from working. Resetting the APN settings to default is a safe and common step that can fix hidden issues.

Let’s go ahead and reset your APN settings to default. After you do this, you’ll need to restart your phone again for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings, or do you know how to do it? Let me know, and I’ll guide you through the process to make sure it’s done right.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...

I went ahead and reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t anything working? I just want excellent internet speed. What else can we try?

Thank you for following all the steps so carefully, John. Since you still have no internet connection after resetting your APN settings, restarting your phone, and confirming you have a strong 5G signal, there may be a deeper technical issue with your line or account that I can’t resolve from here.
